data.title: Walmart+ and Sam’s Club Plus memberships to come bundled in $120 subscription
data.description:
Walmart Inc. will bundle memberships for its Walmart+ and Sam’s Club Plus programs, making a bet that shoppers will subscribe to both when given the chance to save nearly $100.

The paid membership programs for Walmart and its sibling chain of club locations both include free delivery options, as well as lineups of other perks that will be offered together for a $120 annual fee.

Walmart ranks No. 2 in Digital Commerce 360’s Top 1000 Database. The market research tool tracks North America’s largest online retailers by their annual ecommerce sales.

In addition, Walmart is No. 37 in Digital Commerce 360 and ReFiBuy’s AI Commerce Rankings. That set of rankings is available in the Top 1000 Pro with AI Database.

Why Walmart+ and Sam’s Club Plus memberships are being offered together

“We’re giving people a reason to expect more from their memberships,” said John Furner, president and CEO at Walmart. “For $120 a year, we’re raising expectations for what a membership can deliver: more money in their pockets and more time to call their own.”

In a list of features and benefits published by Walmart, the company outlined 26 perks that it would make available, including those from the standalone Walmart+ and Sam’s Club Plus plans, as well as four that do not appear outside of the combined bundle. Those include:

  • Pharmacy savings
  • Savings on optical and hearing
  • Early shopping
  • An annual $60 electronic gift card for T-Mobile

For existing Walmart+ members under the retailer’s annual plan, the combined membership means an additional $22 annual cost. Meanwhile, the company said the Sam’s Club Plus members could add Walmart+ to their existing subscription at no extra cost. Sam’s Club members who do not already pay for Plus will be charged $60 more per year to add both memberships to their accounts.

Benefits from the individual Walmart+ and Sam’s Club Plus memberships

Both Walmart+ and Sam’s Club Plus have added new incentives in recent years, expanding their work with partners to build out benefits to compete with other paid membership programs such as Amazon Prime and Target Circle 360.

In the latest announcement, Walmart highlighted streaming access to either Peacock or Paramount+, as well as savings of 10 cents a gallon at more than 17,000 participating stations, among the combined subscription’s selling points.

Sam’s Club added Weight Watchers options to its program over the summer. In 2024, Walmart incorporated Burger King purchase savings into its memberships.

data.title: Wildfire and Badge bring merchant rewards into Apple, Google and Samsung wallets
data.description:
The loyalty platform Wildfire Systems and mobile wallet infrastructure provider Badge are partnering to push merchant offers and cashback rewards to more shoppers through popular payment methods. The companies announced their partnership at the Money20/20 USA event in Las Vegas.

Together, Wildfire and Badge will allow merchants to extend existing rewards programs to additional payment tools that a customer may already be using. The options will reach both online purchases and purchases in physical stores.

The new deal connects Wildfire’s network of more than 50,000 merchants to Badge’s digital wallet infrastructure, which includes Apple Wallet, Google Wallet and Samsung Wallet. 

How the Wildfire-Badge partnership will work

When a consumer adds a rewards pass to their mobile wallet, it will then surface personalized cashback and savings offers from merchants in Wildfire’s network. As offers change or new deals become relevant, the pass updates automatically. 

Consumers also receive push notifications when new offers are available. The pass can surface location-aware reminders when a shopper is near a participating merchant’s physical store. When the shopper is ready to buy, either online or in store, the offer is prepared and presented to them in their wallet.

Attribution and tracking are handled by Wildfire’s platform on the back end, so neither the merchant nor the loyalty program operator needs to build separate infrastructure to support wallet-based offers.

“Our partnership with Badge gives clients a way to extend their existing rewards programs into mobile wallets, meeting their customers where they are to discover and use offers,” Wildfire CEO Jordan Glazier said in a written statement. “In turn, our merchant network gives Badge’s clients a steady stream of relevant offers to put in front of their customers.”

The system is designed to work across both digital and physical retail. For online purchases, the offer appears in the wallet app and is applied at checkout. For an in-store purchase, the same wallet a consumer taps to pay also carries the relevant cashback offer, connecting the payment moment to the rewards program.

What Wildfire and Badge do with retailers

Wildfire is a commerce intelligence platform that provides retail media and rewards program services for financial services and technology companies. Visa, Citi and RBC are among its clients. Wildfire’s merchants include high-profile retailers such as Best Buy, Macy’s and Ulta Beauty.

Best Buy ranks No. 8 in the Top 1000 Database. The Top 1000 is Digital Commerce 360’s market research tool that tracks North America’s largest online retailers by their annual ecommerce sales. There, Ulta Beauty ranks No. 37, and Macy’s ranks No. 18.

Meanwhile, Badge is a platform that allows clients to make mobile wallets programmable to drive engagement and sales. 

“The next evolution of mobile wallets is about what happens beyond the transaction,” Badge CEO Eric Senn said. “By combining our technology with Wildfire’s merchant offer network, we can help our clients put relevant savings opportunities directly into consumers’ hands, whether they’re shopping online or walking into a store.”

data.title: Bonobos launches Shopify-powered site with omnichannel fit and profile capabilities
data.description:
Menswear brand Bonobos announced the relaunch of its website on Shopify in October. The company cited numerous benefits that it will seek to realize. Examples include faster checkout and new “My Fit” profiles that sync sizing between Bonobos.com and its 48 physical stores, known as Guideshops.

Customers will see a host of new options when visiting Bonobos virtually or in physical stores. As they do, Bonobos hopes to build out its omnichannel capabilities and offerings for those shoppers.

“With Shopify, fit data now syncs across Bonobos.com and our selling systems, giving our Guides a real-time view of customers’ sizing preferences,” Ellen Pope, senior director of ecommerce at Bonobos, told Digital Commerce 360.

Why Bonobos relaunched its ecommerce site with Shopify

Bonobos broke down highlights for the new Shopify site at launch. They include:

  • My Fit profiles: Guides can see a customer’s sizing preferences in real time, and the data syncs with Bonobos.com so size recommendations follow shoppers across channels.
  • Fitting room follow-ups: After a fitting, Bonobos automatically follows up with the customer to keep the service going beyond the visit, which experts point to as an example of engaging the customer to better produce conversions later.
  • Browse online, check out in store: Using Shopify POS, associates can build a complete look with a customer and carry it straight to the in-store register without rebuilding the cart.
  • Cross-channel attribution: A check-in system logs store visits, so a purchase made within seven days, online or in person, is credited to the original store and Guide.
  • One-tap checkout: Shop Pay offers a faster checkout that Shopify says is used by hundreds of millions of buyers worldwide.

Pope told Digital Commerce 360 that the goal of the Shopify work was to create a more connected shopping experience. Together, the companies tried to bring together what customers discover online with the personalized service they receive in the Guideshops. That vision extends beyond the My Fit profiles into the checkout experience and elsewhere.

“We’ve also introduced browse-on-web checkout, which allows a Guide to build a complete look with a customer and bring it directly into the in-store checkout without having to rebuild the cart,” Pope explained.

She added that together, these capabilities make it easier for customers to move between online discovery and in-person service.

Improvements to online shopping experiences

Ultimately, she wants to see the Shopify site help to remove friction and make the experience more experiential and seamless.

“We wanted to make the path from discovering a product to checking out more straightforward. The redesigned experience streamlines the customer journey from product discovery through checkout, while Shop Pay offers an accelerated, one-tap checkout option,” Pope said.

She noted that these updates are designed to make processes easier for customers. If the site works as intended, shoppers should be able to find the right styles, understand fit and complete their purchases with confidence.

The Shopify site’s omnichannel impact

Meanwhile, the My Fit profiles will continue to do work for customers in physical stores, in addition to online.

“Fit has always been central to the Bonobos experience, so we wanted to make sure customers can benefit from that personalized approach wherever they shop,” Pope stated.

She sees My Fit profiles offering Guides a real-time view of customers’ sizing preferences, with fit data syncing across selling systems and Bonobos.com.

“This allows our Guides to make more informed sizing recommendations and helps create a more consistent experience across channels, whether a customer is browsing online or visiting a Guideshop,” Pope said.

Moreover, the Shopify site plays into the company’s broader technology ambitions.

“This launch is an important step in Bonobos’ broader digital transformation, bringing together our digital storefront and the personalized, one-to-one service that has always defined our Guideshops,” Pope said.

She elaborated that by connecting fit data, in-store service and online checkout, she sees Bonobos creating a more seamless experience for customers. Meanwhile, she believes they can give team members a more flexible technology foundation.

“Shopify allows us to continue improving that experience as customer needs evolve, with a focus on making it easier to discover products, find the right fit and shop wherever it’s most convenient,” Pope said.

What the Shopify site is designed to solve for Bonobos

Shopify also weighed in on the new partnership.

“Bonobos built its reputation on getting fit right, and that only works online if the technology can keep up,” said Lauren Nemeth, VP, global enterprise at Shopify. “Our infrastructure is built for that level of product complexity, so brands like Bonobos can spend their energy on the customer experience instead of the infrastructure behind it.”

Chris Ribeiro is the founder of Starlight Analytics and a marketing professor at Rutgers Business School. He said that having a fit profile built in a Guideshop experience with a real person is a logical move. Moreover, he expects the brand will learn more about its customers.

“[Bonobos] now has really great data about its customers to deliver more meaningful and personalized experiences across both channels,” he stated.

Ribeiro said that for Bonobos, those Guideshops have always been about experience and relationship building. In his view, they do not necessarily need to be the place to convert.  The job is to create an omnichannel experience that pays off long term.

“Their job is to make the second, third, and fourth purchase happen online with confidence and to reduce the friction on the business and the customer on size/fit/return processes,” Ribeiro says. “In this space in particular, size and fit are king.”

He says omnichannel customers spend 2-3x more, and 15-35% of online orders get returned.

Potential for My Fit profiles

Meanwhile, Jessica  Murphy, co-founder and CEO of the sizing platform True Fit, assessed that My Fit profiles show promise. She believes that if fit preferences can carry from Bonobos.com into a Guideshop — and back — time to checkout could shorten.

“Fit confidence helps someone decide what to buy and feel good keeping it,” she said. “Those are two different problems, and brands often measure only the first.”

Murphy added that conversion rising while shoppers keep what they buy will be important. Potentially, it could provide stronger evidence of reduced friction than a faster transaction alone.

Still, Murphy said that there are a lot of variables even in the most seamless experiences.

“A profile only helps if it reflects what the shopper wants now and the product in front of them,” she noted. “A 32×32 in one chino is not a 32×32 in a new fabric or a slimmer cut.”

She emphasized that cut, fabric and desired ease still matter.

“So the profile should inform the recommendation, not replace product-specific guidance,” Murphy stated.

Last, Murphy anticipates there will be signs to watch beyond profile adoption or conversion alone. Those variables may include checkout completion, online and in-store conversion, repeat cross-channel purchases, keep rate, exchanges and fit-related returns.

“Conversion rising while shoppers keep what they buy is stronger evidence of reduced friction than a faster transaction alone,” Murphy said. “The concept is promising, but the setup alone is not proof of a sales lift. The impact needs to be measured.”

data.title: David's Bridal plans to spin off its AI-powered Pearl platform
data.description:
In 2025, David’s Bridal’s Shopify transition paved the way for an agentic artificial intelligence (AI) reimagining of its Pearl wedding planner — and now, the company has plans to spin off Pearl as its own entity.

K&F Growth Acquisition Corp. II, as special purposed acquisition company, announced alongside David’s Bridal, that the two companies had signed a nonbinding letter of intent to carry out a process to that would see Pearl go public.

Ultimately, their plan also calls for Pearl to eventually own David’s Bridal’s brand and intellectual property.

David’s Bridal is No. 460 in the Top 1000 Database. The market research tool tracks North America’s largest online retailers, ranking them by annual ecommerce sales and more.

David’s Bridal is also No. 178 in Digital Commerce 360 and ReFiBuy’s AI Commerce Rankings. That set of rankings is available in the Top 1000 Pro with AI Database.

data.title: Salesforce to acquire Braze for $5.66 billion to expand AI-powered marketing
data.description:
Salesforce plans to acquire Braze for $5.66 billion, making an artificial intelligence (AI) play for technology to help brands respond to shopper behavior in real time.

Under the definitive agreement announced Oct. 20, Braze shareholders would receive $47.50 per share in cash. That represents a roughly 58% premium over the stock’s Oct. 19 closing price.

Salesforce expects the acquisition to strengthen its Marketing Cloud business and broader AI offerings.

“Braze was built to turn live customer behavior into personalized engagement at scale,” said Patrick Stokes, president of applications and marketing at Salesforce, in the acquisition announcement. “Bringing that capability together with Salesforce Marketing Cloud, CRM and Data 360 will deliver that wow moment in every customer interaction.”

The transaction is expected to close during Salesforce’s fiscal 2028, which runs from Feb. 1, 2027, through Jan. 31, 2028. The deal remains subject to shareholder and regulatory approvals. Salesforce said it does not expect the acquisition to affect its fiscal 2027 financial guidance.

In North America, 78 of the Top 2000 online retailers use Salesforce as their ecommerce platform, according to Digital Commerce 360 data. Together, those retailers generated more than $192.60 billion in web sales in 2025. The Top 2000 is Digital Commerce 360’s database ranking North America’s largest online retailers by annual ecommerce sales.

What Salesforce gains from Braze’s AI capabilities

New York-based Braze specializes in personalized marketing across mobile apps, websites, email and other digital channels. Using real-time customer data and AI, its platform helps brands optimize the message, timing and channel for customer interactions.

Braze would bring considerable scale to Salesforce’s marketing business. Its platform serves roughly 2,770 customers, including Urban Outfitters, Instacart and Canva. Urban Outfitters is No. 29 in the Top 2000.

In a LinkedIn post on Oct. 20, Braze co-founder and chief technology officer Jon Hyman shared that the platform engages 9 billion monthly active users across its customer base. In 2025, Braze also handled “about 4.5 trillion messages and other actions to consumers,” he wrote.

A key part of the deal is BrazeAI, which combines predictive, generative and agentic AI. According to Braze, the tools can anticipate customer behavior, generate marketing content and optimize when, where and how brands reach shoppers.

How Salesforce plans to integrate Braze

For Salesforce, Braze could fill a gap in its existing marketing business.

The acquisition would give Salesforce “a real-time engagement layer that its marketing business has historically lacked,” Shay Boloor, chief market strategist at Futurum Equities, told Reuters.

Salesforce plans to connect Braze’s real-time marketing technology with Customer 360, its suite of customer data and applications spanning sales, marketing, commerce and service. The ecommerce platform and software provider expects the combination to strengthen Marketing Cloud, which businesses use to manage marketing campaigns.

With access to Salesforce’s customer data, Braze’s technology could help marketers “adapt engagement as customers browse, buy, and use products,” according to the acquisition announcement.

Salesforce also expects Braze’s AI capabilities to work alongside Agentforce, its platform for deploying AI agents that can make decisions and carry out tasks. The combination could help businesses better coordinate marketing with ecommerce, sales and customer service, Salesforce said.

Meanwhile, Braze CEO and co-founder Bill Magnuson said Salesforce’s technology, reach and partner network would help the company “bring more of our vision to market sooner.”

In an Oct. 20 LinkedIn post, Magnuson also said he would remain CEO and that the company would continue operating as Braze.

How retailers are using Braze to drive sales

Some retailers are already reporting higher engagement and conversion rates from campaigns using Braze’s technology.

Grove Collaborative, a sustainability-focused online retailer, switched to Braze after its previous marketing platform couldn’t support real-time personalization. The system had also crashed on Thanksgiving Eve, according to a Braze case study.

Integrating Braze with its Shopify storefront allowed Grove to automate personalized reminders and product suggestions for shoppers who browsed without buying. The resulting campaign generated a 10% checkout rate, a 41% add-to-cart rate and a 3% click-through rate, according to Braze.

E.l.f. Beauty Inc. offers another example. The beauty retailer partnered with Braze and Stitch to expand its mobile marketing efforts and boost engagement with its loyalty program, Beauty Squad.

With help from the two companies, e.l.f. expanded its use of push notifications and personalized in-app campaigns to encourage customers to return to its mobile app. Between March and September 2023, monthly mobile app usage increased 125%, according to a separate Braze case study.

The retailer also added push notifications to its existing loyalty emails, reminding Beauty Squad members to redeem rewards before they expired. Those efforts, alongside other support from Braze, contributed to a 58% year-over-year increase in loyalty offer redemptions in 2024, according to the study.

Grove ranks No. 256 in the Top 2000, while e.l.f. Beauty ranks No. 328.

Salesforce expands AI capabilities through acquisitions

The Braze deal is part of Salesforce’s push to expand its AI offerings through in-house development and acquisitions.

That strategy comes as Salesforce’s existing AI business gains traction. In its fiscal second quarter, Agentforce annual recurring revenue surpassed $1.5 billion, up 240% year over year. Combined with Data 360, annual recurring revenue reached $3.9 billion, according to the company’s earnings results.

Meanwhile, the company has made several other sizable acquisitions this year. In September, it completed its $3.6 billion deal to acquire Fin, which develops AI agents for handling customer service inquiries.

That same month, it acquired Contentful for roughly $1.5 billion to support more personalized customer experiences.

More recently, Salesforce announced an agreement to acquire Listen Labs, which uses AI agents to conduct customer research and analyze feedback. Financial terms were not disclosed.
